units.zh: 高麗、渤海因之。

units.zh: 至遼，五京列峙、包括燕、代，悉為畿甸。
units.en: Under Liao the five capitals stood in a row, embracing Yan and Dai as the metropolitan heartland.
units.literal: By Liao, with the five capitals arrayed side by side embracing Yan and Dai, all became metropolitan domains.

units.zh: 二百餘年，城郭相望，田野益辟。
units.en: For over two centuries walled towns lined the landscape and farmland spread.
units.literal: Over more than two hundred years cities faced one another and fields opened ever wider.

units.zh: 冠以節度，承以觀察、防禦、團練等使，分以刺史、縣令，大略采用唐制。
units.en: Military commissioners headed circuits, observation, defense, and training commissioners followed, and cishi and magistrates filled the counties—largely on the Tang model.
units.literal: Crowned with military commissioners, continued with observation, defense, and regional training commissioners, and divided among cishi and magistrates—broadly adopting Tang institutions.

units.zh: 其間宗室、外戚、大臣之家，築城賜額，謂之「頭下州軍」；
units.en: Imperial kin, in-laws, and great ministers also founded walled estates with granted names—the "head-below prefectures and armies";
units.literal: Meanwhile imperial clansmen, maternal kin, and great ministers' households built walled settlements and received designations, called "head-below prefectures and armies";

units.zh: 唯節度使朝廷命之，後往往皆歸王府。
units.en: only military commissioners were court-appointed, but in time most posts fell to princely households.
units.literal: only military commissioners were appointed by the court, yet in time they mostly reverted to princely establishments.

units.zh: 不能州者謂之軍，不能縣者謂之城，不能城者謂之堡。
units.en: Units too small for a prefecture became armies; too small for a county became cities; too small for a city became forts.
units.literal: Where a prefecture could not be formed it was called an army; where a county could not be formed it was called a city; where a city could not be formed it was called a fort.

units.en: Bankrupt households could not meet levies, to the distress of the people.

units.literal: They settled ordinary cases, gathered hidden grievances of the people; since Han and Tang, worthy rulers have treated this as the standing statute for cherishing the people.

units.zh: 官不常設，有詔，則選材望官為之。

units.literal: The Liao state took herding, farming, and fishing as its staple production; fiscal offices at first were very simple.

units.literal: From Nieli's teaching of plowing and weaving, salt, iron, and other profits daily multiplied; once Yan and Dai were taken, the realm grew still richer.

units.en: The ancient sage-kings were gentle; their grace extended through Han and Tang.
units.literal: The Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors ruled with leniency; their beneficence reached Han and Tang.

units.zh: 好生惡殺，習與性成。
units.en: Love of life and hatred of killing were second nature.
units.literal: Cherishing life and hating killing became habit and nature.

units.zh: 雖五代極亂，習於戰鬥者才幾人耳。
units.en: Even Five Dynasties chaos produced few habitual warriors.
units.literal: Even in the extreme disorder of the Five Dynasties, those practiced in battle were only a few men.

units.zh: 宋以文勝，然遼之邊防猶重於南面，直以其地大民眾故耳。
units.en: Song won by civil culture, but Liao still stressed the southern frontier because of its size and population.
units.literal: Song prevailed through culture, yet Liao frontier defense still weighed more on the Southern Face, simply because that region was vast and populous.

units.zh: 卒之親仁善鄰，桴鼓不鳴幾二百年。
units.en: Finally, benevolence and good neighbors kept the drums quiet for nearly two centuries.
units.literal: In the end, through cherishing benevolence and good neighborliness, war drums were silent for nearly two hundred years.

units.zh: 此遼之所以為美也歟。
units.en: That was Liao's glory.
units.literal: This is why Liao was admirable indeed.
